title: CRO Lead
description:
**OneMetric \| Full\-time \| Gurgaon**

**The role in one line**
------------------------


This is not a "manage the website" role or a CRO role for its own sake — it's a lead\-generation role that uses the website as the primary lever. You own the website end to end — from a raw idea for a page to a shipped, converting landing page — against one defined outcome: 35–50 MQLs a month generated organically from the website and the motions around it.

**Why this role exists**
------------------------


Most people who "manage the website" either write copy and hand it to a designer, or build pages and wait for someone else to tell them what to put on them. We need someone who does both halves in one head: knows what a page needs to say because they've done the research and talked to customers, and knows why a page converts or doesn't because they think like a CRO person, not just a writer or a builder. The output is a live, working page — not a doc that someone else has to translate.

**What you'll own**
-------------------

* **The website as a whole** — structure, page inventory, and how it evolves as the company's positioning evolves.
* **Idea**  **live page.** You take a rough brief ("we need a page for X service" or "we're repositioning around Y") and turn it into a wireframe, then real copy, then a shipped page — working with a designer where needed, but driving the thing yourself.
* **Conversion performance** — what's converting, what isn't, and why. You run the experiments, not just report the numbers.
* **Lead capture and funnel logic on\-site** — forms, CTAs, gating, the path from a visitor landing on a page to becoming a lead in HubSpot.
* **The lead number.** 35–50 organic leads/month from the website and the motions around it (SEO, AEO, on\-site conversion, content) is your number. The page isn't done when it ships — it's done when it's producing.

**What you'll actually do, week to week**
-----------------------------------------

* Talk to customers and internal stakeholders (sales, delivery, leadership) to figure out what a page actually needs to say to move a buyer — not guess at it from a template.
* Look at signals — search intent, competitor positioning, what prospects ask sales, what's converting elsewhere — and turn them into a point of view on what the page should be.
* Write the copy yourself. This isn't a hand\-off role — strong, clear, buyer\-facing writing is a core skill here, not a nice\-to\-have.
* Sketch wireframes and work directly with a designer (or design tools yourself) to get from idea to a real, live example fast.
* Build and manage pages in WordPress and HubSpot CMS.
* Use AI tools (Claude and others) and Figma as part of your everyday workflow — for research, drafting, quick mockups, and design iteration.
* Structure pages and content for both traditional SEO and AEO (answer engine optimization) — so the site shows up in Google *and* gets cited by AI answer engines like ChatGPT, Perplexity, and AI Overviews.
* Track what's converting and what's not, and keep iterating rather than treating a page as "done" once it ships.

**What we need**
----------------

* **A CRO brain.** You should be able to look at a page and say, with reasons, why it will or won't convert — and know how to fix it. This means understanding funnels, lead capture mechanics, and what actually moves a B2B buyer to act.
* **Strong writing, in service of strategy.** You can write clean, persuasive copy, but more importantly you know *what* needs to be said and *why*, before you write a word.
* **A founder/CMO\-level eye for B2B design.** You don't need to be the designer, but you need the taste to know what good B2B design looks like and the ability to brief and push back on one.
* **The ability to simplify.** You can take a genuinely complex service or technical concept (a RevOps build, an AI GTM agent) and explain it in language a buyer actually understands.
* **A working understanding of AEO and SEO.** You know how to structure and write content so it ranks in search *and* gets picked up and cited by AI answer engines (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews) — this isn't optional anymore for a website role.
* **Strong writing skills paired with AI fluency.** You write well yourself, and you use AI tools to move fast — generating quick mockups, drafts, and iterations rather than waiting on a full design cycle for every idea.
* **Comfort with the tools**: WordPress, HubSpot CMS, Figma, and AI tools (Claude and similar) as part of daily work.
* **Ownership instinct** — you treat the website as yours, not as a queue of tickets from other teams.
* 4–5 years of experience working on websites/landing pages, ideally with direct exposure to conversion work, not just content or design in isolation.

**What's in it for you**
------------------------

* **Ownership, not a task list.** We don't hand you a checklist and check boxes. Direction and context get discussed openly, and then the "how" — the wireframe, the copy, the page — is yours to run with.
* **A performance\-driven culture.** Speed and conversion results define your trajectory here, not tenure or face\-time. Ship fast, see what moves the numbers, and get rewarded for it.
* **Access to the top of the market.** The pages you build speak to CMOs, VPs of Sales, and founders across the B2B US market — real high\-stakes work, not busywork nobody reads.

**How we'll know this is working**
----------------------------------


Within a quarter: organic leads from the website and its motions are trending toward the 35–50/month range, pages you've shipped are outperforming what existed before on conversion, sales and leadership are coming to you first when a new page or repositioning is needed, and the website stops feeling like a static asset and starts feeling like something that's actively working for the business.

**Who you'll work with**
------------------------


Reports into growth/marketing leadership at OneMetric, works closely with sales, delivery leads, and a designer (in\-house or external) to take ideas from brief to live page.

**Who you'll work with**
------------------------


This role reports to the CEO’s office at OneMetric and works closely with sales and delivery leaders on HubSpot implementation, RevOps, and GTM projects.

title: Content Marketer - BOFU
description:
**OneMetric \| Full\-time \| Gurgaon**

**Quick summary:**
------------------


Take charge of everything that turns a warm lead into a closed deal. This includes the content, the sequence, and the journey each lead follows. You’ll be responsible for generating 20–30 MQLs each month from your efforts.

**Why are we introducing this role?**
-------------------------------------


Most content writers stop at just writing the case study. We need someone who writes the case study, understands why the client made a purchase, builds the email sequence it belongs in, decides which segment sees it and when, and can explain whether it helped move the pipeline. You will design the funnel yourself, from mid\-funnel nurture all the way to closed\-won deals.

**What you'll own.**
--------------------

* **BOFU content includes** case studies, white papers, sales one\-pagers, comparison or battlecard content, and ROI stories. These should be written with enough conviction and detail that a business leader, not just a marketer, reads it and finds it believable.
* **You’ll create** outbound email sequences, sales follow\-up routines, newsletter\-to\-sale paths, and the logic for segmenting who receives what and when.
* **Your goal is to generate 20–30 MQLs** per month from BOFU content and journeys. You’re not just creating assets; you’re responsible for the results they deliver.
* **You’ll work closely** with delivery, sales, and subject\-matter experts to truly understand the work, such as HubSpot implementations, RevOps builds, and GTM projects. This way, you can write about these topics with real credibility, not just from a brief.

**What you'll actually do, week to week**
-----------------------------------------

* **You’ll interview internal teams** (delivery, sales, leadership) and clients to uncover the real story behind a win. Then, you’ll turn that story into a case study or white paper that feels genuine, not like generic marketing content.
* **You’ll build and improve BOFU email sequences** and nurture journeys in HubSpot, as well as use tools like Dripify for outbound campaigns.
* **You’ll design the logic for** segmentation, deciding who enters which journey, based on specific signals and stages.
* **You’ll write outbound sales emails** that are compelling enough for founders or CMOs to respond to.
* **You’ll track what’s working,** stop what isn’t, and report on your MQL results each month.
* **You’ll work directly with sales to learn what content actually** helps them close deals, and you’ll create content that supports those needs, not just fill a content calendar.

**What we need**
----------------

* **We want writing that shows conviction, not just template copy. You should be able to** take a technical project, like a CRM migration or RevOps build, and write about it with a clear point of view. Your writing should be the kind that makes a business leader stop and pay attention.
* **You need real experience in B2B marketing, RevOps, or GTM.** It’s not enough to have just written for B2B before. You should understand funnels, lead lifecycles, MQL andSQL definitions, and how BOFU content supports the sales process.
* **You should be able to design funnels and journeys, including** segmentation, sequencing, and stage logic. You need to be comfortable sketching out a journey on a whiteboard, not just writing the copy for it.
* **Working proficiency with HubSpot** (workflows, sequences, lists/segmentatiYou should be comfortable doing the legwork. This role means you’ll go out and get the information you need by talking to engineers, delivery leads, and clients, instead of waiting for a content brief.rather than waiting for a content brief.
* We prefer candidates with 3 to 6 years of experience in B2B content or demand generation, ideally from an agency or SaaS background.

**Good to have:**
-----------------

* It’s a plus if you have experience writing for a services or consultancy business, such as a HubSpot partner, RevOps agency, or martech consultancy, rather than just for product SaaS.

**What's in it for you**
------------------------

* **Here, you get real ownership instead of just a list of tasks.** We talk openly about direction and context, but you decide how to get things done. If you prefer having every step defined for you, this might not be the right place. But if you like working with clear goals and plenty of freedom, you'll fit right in.
* **We have a performance\-driven culture.** Your progress depends on how quickly you work and the results you deliver, not on how long you've been here or how much time you spend at your desk. Move fast and show what you can do, and you'll be recognised.
* **You'll have the chance to work** directly with CMOs, VPs of Sales, and founders across the B2B US market. Instead of creating content in isolation, you'll help shape projects for some of the top go\-to\-market leaders. Knowing the US market well will really help you succeed here.

**How we'll know this is working**
----------------------------------


You’ll see results within a quarter. MQLs from BOFU content and sequences should be moving toward 20–30 per month. Sales will ask you for more of the assets that are working, and the case studies or white papers you create will be the ones sales teams use in their emails without being prompted.

**Who you'll work with**
------------------------


This role reports to the CEO’s office at OneMetric and works closely with sales and delivery leaders on HubSpot implementation, RevOps, and GTM projects.
